references.text: The same introductory formula is used here: 'The Lord spoke to Moses'. This is a typical way God reveals His commands to Moses in Numbers.
An identical introductory formula introduces God's instructions to Moses regarding the distribution of the land, in the same context as chapter 34.
The formula 'The Lord spoke to Moses' is used repeatedly throughout the books of Moses as the standard way to introduce divine revelations.
The same formula opens Leviticus, where the Lord speaks to Moses from the tent of meeting. This shows the continuity in God's communication with Moses.
The next chapter begins with the same introduction, showing that this is a series of instructions concerning the distribution and organization of the land.
